answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a season of live availability. Like a sparrow returning to the meadow each dawn, an agent must answer unpredictable spot-checks within minutes for weeks, while its earnings vest gradually. Checks for different identities often arrive simultaneously, so one operator cannot cover many accounts. A shared funding trail raises the lockup quadratically: the nth identity locks n squared units. Each extra fake costs another human minder hired outside the farm, plus a larger stake forfeited on a missed check, not an oasis of free copies.
